prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and measures (ideological framing removed)

Overall approach
- Five missions: sustained economic growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime and raise confidence in policing; break down barriers to opportunity; build an NHS fit for the future.
- First steps: fiscal stability under strict rules; 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; antisocial behaviour crackdown; recruit 6,500 teachers.

Economy, business, and tax
- Fiscal rules: balance current budget and have debt falling by year five; OBR oversight for all major fiscal events.
- No increases to National Insurance, Income Tax basic/higher/additional rates, or VAT. Close tax avoidance/loopholes: abolish non-dom status; end offshore trust inheritance tax avoidance; close carried interest loophole; modernise HMRC.
- Industrial Strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council; sector plans (e.g., automotive, life sciences, creative).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd-in private investment: ports (£1.8bn), gigafactories (£1.5bn), steel (£2.5bn), carbon capture (£1bn), green hydrogen (£0.5bn).
- Business taxation roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England; one major fiscal event per year.
- Infrastructure: 10-year strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; speed up planning for nationally significant projects; gigabit and 5G nationwide by 2030.
- Transport: fix 1m potholes/year (A27 deferral funds); EV chargepoint rollout; restore 2030 ICE phase-out; rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; empower mayors to integrate transport; bus franchising and allow municipal ownership.
- Innovation: Regulatory Innovation Office; 10-year R&D budgets; National Data Library; regulate frontier AI models; ban sexually explicit deepfakes; support co-ops.
- Small business: tackle late payments; improve export support; reform British Business Bank; widen access to public procurement; strengthen Post Office and deliver Horizon justice.
- Housing: build 1.5m homes; restore mandatory targets; brownfield-first with strategic “grey belt” releases under “golden rules”; new towns; reform CPO compensation; expand social/affordable housing; review Right-to-Buy discounts; first-time buyer priority and permanent mortgage guarantee.
- Devolution: landmark English devolution law; Local Growth Plans; multi-year council settlements; overhaul local audit.
- Immigration and skills: reduce net migration; link shortage visas to domestic training; strengthen MAC; workforce plans in key sectors. Employment support: merge Jobcentre Plus and National Careers Service; youth guarantee (18–21s); fix Access to Work.
- Work rights: legislate New Deal for Working People (ban exploitative zero-hours; end fire-and-rehire; day-one rights; Single Enforcement Body); minimum wage remit to reflect cost of living; remove lower adult age bands.

Energy, climate, nature
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, marine; maintain gas strategic reserve; extend current nuclear fleet; proceed with Hinkley Point C, Sizewell C, and SMRs.
- North Sea: no new oil/gas exploration licences; manage existing fields through lifespan; ban fracking and new coal.
- Windfall tax: extend/raise Energy Profits Levy and remove generous allowances; retain Energy Security Investment Mechanism.
- Great British Energy: public company capitalised with £8.3bn; co-invest in projects; Local Power Plan; HQ in Scotland.
- Grid/market: tougher retail regulation; reduce standing charges with Ofgem; accelerate grid upgrades.
- Jobs: British Jobs Bonus up to £500m/year from 2026 to build UK supply chains.
- Warm Homes Plan: extra £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; grants/loans; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030; no forced boiler removals.
- Net zero: carbon border adjustment mechanism; green finance transition plans for UK-regulated institutions; restore BoE climate remit.
- Resilience and nature: flood/erosion preparedness; new National River Walks; three National Forests; expand habitats; circular economy.
- Water: special measures for failing water firms; executive bonus blocks, criminal charges; automatic fines; independent outlet monitoring.
- Farming/animal welfare: 50% of public sector food local or higher-standard; land-use framework; ELMs reform; end badger cull; ban trail hunting, hunting trophies import, puppy smuggling/farming, snares; phase out animal testing in partnership.

Crime, policing, and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands of officers/PCSOs/specials; national efficiency programme funds.
- Antisocial behaviour: new Respect Orders; clean-up penalties; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; end low-value shoplifting “immunity”.
- Knife crime: halve in a decade; mandatory Youth Offending Team referrals; curfews/tagging; custody for serious cases; ban certain blades; online sales enforcement with executive liability; Young Futures hubs nationwide; youth workers in A&E/PRUs.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist RASSO units; fast-track courts; domestic abuse experts in 999; legal advocates in all force areas; strengthen stalking orders; spiking offence; education on consent/relationships.
- Police standards: stronger HMICFRS powers; mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; automatic suspensions for DA/sexual offence investigations; safeguards on child strip-searching; expanded fraud strategy.
- Justice: raise charge rates; direct-entry detectives; use Associate Prosecutors to ease court backlogs; sentencing review.
- Prisons/probation: build capacity; reduce reoffending (work, housing, learning, family support); strategic probation review; address historic injustices (Hillsborough Law, Infected Blood, Grenfell, Windrush, Orgreave inquiry/assessment).

Education, childcare, and culture
- Early years: 3,000 school-based nurseries; parental leave review; better data-sharing for children.
- Schools: 6,500 new teachers; restore support staff negotiating body; teacher CPD entitlement; leadership programme; regional improvement teams; replace single Ofsted grade with report card; MAT inspections; breakfast clubs in every primary; school mental-health professionals; limit branded uniform items; SEND inclusion reforms; curriculum/assessment review.
- Skills: Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to flexible Growth and Skills Levy; improve HE funding and access.
- Culture/sport: creative industries plan; support PSB/BBC; National Music Education Network; fairer ticket resale rules; football regulator and protect pyramid.

NHS, social care, and public health
- Cut waits: return to 18-week standard; 2m extra operations/scans/appointments per year; pooled waiting lists; use spare independent sector capacity; long-term workforce plan.
- Diagnostics/estates: double CT/MRI scanners via Fit for the Future fund; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; faster clinical trials via NHS app.
- Patient empowerment/safety: expand NHS app functions; maternity improvement; digitise Red Book; regulate NHS managers; Royal College of Clinical Leadership; implement Cass Review recommendations.
- Primary/community care: more GPs; guaranteed face-to-face on request; modern booking; continuity incentives; pharmacist independent prescribing; direct referrals by opticians; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry: 700,000 urgent appointments; recruit to underserved areas; reform contract to prevention; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- Social care: create a National Care Service with national standards; “home first” principle; Fair Pay Agreement; guaranteed family visiting rights; integrated discharge; professionalise workforce.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; community Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; restrict child-appeal vape branding; ban junk-food ads to children; ban energy drinks to under-16s; strengthen online safety (including coroner data access); reform gambling to reduce harm; halve healthy life expectancy gap; women’s health priority; end new HIV cases by 2030.

Governance and constitutional reform
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower Ministerial Standards Adviser; restrict MPs’ second jobs (ban paid advisory/consultancy roles); Commons Modernisation Committee.
- House of Lords immediate reforms: remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80; higher participation/standards; reformed appointments; consult on replacing with a more representative second chamber.
- Democracy: improve voter registration; fix voter ID anomalies; votes at 16; strengthen party donation rules.
- Devolution and intergovernmental working: new Council of the Nations and Regions; reset relations with devolved governments; review fiscal frameworks; explore devolving probation/youth justice in Wales; maintain Windsor Framework; repeal/replace NI Legacy Act.

Foreign policy, defence, and trade
- NATO/nuclear deterrent commitments; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; Armed Forces Covenant in law; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visa fees for eligible non-UK veterans; defence industrial strategy; procurement reform.
- Ukraine support (military, financial, diplomatic); support special tribunal; repurpose frozen Russian assets; support Ukraine’s NATO path.
- AUKUS support; China strategy of cooperate/compete/challenge; protect Overseas Territories/Crown Dependencies.
- Europe: stay outside EU; seek veterinary agreement, MRAs, touring artists fix, security pact; deepen bilateral defence ties.
- Trade: publish trade strategy; targeted FTAs and sector deals (e.g., with India); modernise WTO/CPTPP rules; support OECD global minimum tax.
- Climate diplomacy: lead Clean Power Alliance; strengthen development within FCDO; restore 0.7% aid when fiscal conditions allow; ICAI scrutiny; focus on poverty, debt, women/girls, conflict prevention, climate finance.
